label: What this is
text: Data Wrangler. Round up your data and documents, and load them into the DataView database. Every tool can read your documents now — the difference is what happens to what they say. Data Wrangler puts it somewhere you can defend, and refuses to put in what it cannot prove. This is a short tour of the page. Everything described here is shown running in the films further down.

label: Wrong is worse than missing
text: Start with the position everything else follows from. Wrong is worse than missing. A confident wrong value plots on a map, exports to a spreadsheet, and gets quoted in a meeting. A missing one is visible. So a file here has exactly four states, and they are never collapsed into a percentage. Loaded — its rows are in the database. Staged — extracted, and waiting. Held — blocked, with a named reason you can act on. Or nothing at all, which is the only real failure.

label: Reads, writes, exports
text: What it reads: well logs in LAS, DLIS and LIS. Seismic in SEG-Y and P190. Esri shapefiles. Scout tickets, end of well reports and completion records as Word, Excel and PDF. What it writes: SQL Server, Oracle or Snowflake. And what it exports: scout tickets, C S V, multi-page Excel, a PPDM extract, GeoJSON, shapefile, Petrel, GeoGraphix, an OSDU manifest, or a direct write into another database.

label: The components
text: Seven modules, each doing one job and handing its result to the next. DataView is the database — derived from PPDM three point nine, but easier to load into and to customise, and it carries the provenance of every row, so the file a value came from can be opened. The File Catalog is an extension of that same schema: tables for the files on a shared drive and for what was extracted from them. The Data Assistant bulk loads flat files and remembers the mapping, so the second file of a format takes a few clicks. The Document Assistant learns to recognise tables by their shape — and that part is not petroleum specific; it works on any document with tables in it. Mapping is the front end. MapBox and QGIS were both tried and were too slow, so the map was built to fit: three point nine million federated wells, each linked to its documents, and no SQL required.

label: The films
text: Below this you will find five walkthroughs — nineteen minutes, recorded against a live database, nothing mocked and nothing sped up. Every number spoken in them is a number on the screen at the time. The File Catalog film is the one to start with: a full run over a hundred and eighty two files, ending with an empty backlog.
